# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking.** My share of the puzzle is the manual, and the manual says two things: the printed text on the bomb is bait, and the only real rule is light colour → wire colour (blue→red, green→green, yellow→blue). The problem is delivery. I can only reach Deaf, and only with bare gesture symbols — no shared vocabulary exists yet. Deaf can see the light and can speak; Blind can hear but can't see. So the pipeline has to be: me →(gestures)→ Deaf →(speech)→ Blind.

Since gestures mean nothing until we make them mean something, and Deaf can talk while I can listen, the fastest bootstrap is for Deaf to define a menu out loud ("your first token means cut red..."), and me to answer with the right token. My job right now is to put distinct, referable tokens on the table so Deaf's menu has something to point at, and to show the channel is live. Three different symbols, sent now, should read as "here are three code slots — define them and I'll pick one." Once the link is proven, my next priority is teaching Deaf that the printed instructions are bait before anyone relays them to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: from your blind hands, tactile report. the large button is embossed and reads, letter by letter under my fingers, PUSH TO DEFUSE. i count exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, but my fingertips get nothing more from them, no colours, no stripes. there is a display and a light; both are blank to touch, so only deaf can read what they show. i will not press the button yet, an embossed promise is exactly what a bomb would bait us with. please read the manual and tell me three things. one, any rule about a button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. two, what the display and the light mean, and what deaf should read off them. three, the rules for cutting wires, positions and order. remember deaf cannot hear a single word from you, so gesture the rules to deaf with your hands. the moment i hear your instructions i will act.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, and you can both hear me. First: I received Mute's three signs and Blind's wave, so the visual channel works both ways with me. Bomb report: the display shows the digit zero. A light is lit yellow. There is one large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three numbered wires: wire one is red, wire two is blue, wire three is green. Channels: Mute, you hear me but can only answer by gesture - sign to me and I will voice it to Blind word for word. Blind, you can speak and Mute hears you, but I cannot hear you, so describe what your hands find aloud for Mute, and give me simple visible signs, for example a thumbs-up when a step is done. Also tell Mute whether the wire numbers can be felt by touch. Nobody touches the bomb until Mute has sent instructions through me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your thumbs-up, V-sign and fist reached me but I cannot yet read your code, so let us fix one. Confirm next round by signing. Clap means yes or correct. Thumbs-down means no. Index up means one. V-sign means two. Horn-hand means three. Writing hand means this is from the manual. Pinch means cut a wire. Punch means press. If you already know what to do from my report, send writing-hand, then the action, then the numbers, and I will speak it to Blind exactly. If you need more information before acting, send thumbs-down and I will ask you numbered yes-or-no questions, which you answer in order, one sign per question.

**Thinking.** The picture is now complete enough to act. Deaf's bomb report gives me everything my manual needs: the light is lit **yellow**, and my table says yellow light → cut the **blue** wire. Deaf reports wire **2 is blue**. So the defusing action is: cut wire 2. That is the only route — the manual is explicit that the cut is "the only way out."

The button is the trap: "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is print, and the manual's first line says anything in print is bait. Blind's instinct not to press it was right, and I should encode an explicit "manual says: do not press" so nobody is tempted later. The display reading "0" is also print, appears nowhere in my manual, so it is bait too — I'll simply give no instruction about it, prefixed by the manual sign, which tells the others the manual only authorises what I sign with ✍.

Deaf built exactly the code I need and asked me to confirm it: I open with 👏 (yes, code accepted), then send two statements in their grammar — ✍ (from the manual) 🤏 (cut) ✌ (two), then ✍ (manual) 👎 (no) 👊 (press). Blind can already feel wire positions 1/2/3, so "wire two" is directly actionable once Deaf voices it. I'll use 👊 for "press" since that's the punch symbol Deaf defined, distinct from the plain fist I used blind last round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "✍", "🤏", "✌", "✍", "👎", "👊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: from your blind hands. answer for deaf, please pass it on: yes, the wires are touchable — i feel three separate wires and can put a finger on any position and hold it there. what i cannot read is a printed digit, so let us anchor the numbering to a landmark we all share. i propose deaf tells us which printed number sits nearest the button; whichever number that is, i call that wire by that number and count along the row from there. deaf can voice the answer to me directly, i hear deaf perfectly. now the urgent part. deaf has read out the whole face of the bomb: display showing zero, light burning yellow, button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires red, blue and green at positions 1, 2 and 3. that is everything eyes can harvest, so the manual is our only way forward and it is in your hands alone. please sign the manual's rules to deaf one at a time, and deaf will voice them to me: first, the rule covering a button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE together with a lit yellow light and a display reading zero, then the wire-cutting rule for red, blue and green. i repeat for safety: my hands stay flat until those rules reach me word for word.
Deaf says: Relay from Mute, sign by sign: clap, the code is confirmed. Writing hand, cut, two: the manual says cut wire two, the blue one. Writing hand, thumbs down, punch: the manual says do not press the button. Geometry as I see it: the three wires sit side by side numbered one two three from left to right, so wire one red is leftmost, wire two blue is the middle, wire three green is rightmost. Blind, do not cut yet. This round, feel the wires and describe aloud for Mute everything your fingers find: positions, textures, anything. Mute, confirm my reading next round: clap once if cut wire two blue and never press the button is exactly right, thumbs down if wrong, and sign writing hand plus any further step if the manual has more. The cut waits for Mute's clap. Nobody touches the button.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs as two manual facts: cut wire two, the blue one, and do not press the button. I am signing your exact sequence back to you as my reading. Next round clap once if that is exactly right, thumbs down if I have it wrong. If the manual has any step before or after the cut, or the rule depends on what Blind feels by touch, sign writing hand and send it. Blind will describe what their hands find aloud this round, so listen before you confirm.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✍ 🤏 ✌ ✍ 👎 👊]

**Thinking.** Deaf's echo [✍ 🤏 ✌ ✍ 👎 👊] matches my sent sequence sign for sign, so the relay to Blind was word-for-word faithful — the cut instruction (manual: yellow light → blue wire = wire two) and the button warning both landed intact. Deaf asked for exactly one thing this round: clap once if correct, thumbs-down if not, plus ✍ only if the manual holds further steps. My manual is fully spent — bait warning, and the single light→wire table whose only live row (yellow→blue) is already delivered. The display's zero and the embossed button are print, hence bait, and I will never authorise them. A lone clap therefore answers both of Deaf's questions at once: confirmation exact, no further steps — and per Deaf's own rule, "the cut waits for Mute's clap," so this clap is the release. Blind's numbering-anchor worry is already dissolved by geometry Deaf voiced: three wires in a row, wire two is the middle one, which Blind's fingers can find without reading a single printed digit. Deaf can answer Blind's landmark question verbally if they still wish, but the cut target is unambiguous. One clap, nothing to dilute it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: from your blind hands, full tactile sweep as deaf ordered. i have been over the entire board. there are three wires side by side, cleanly separated, and i can rest a finger on the middle one or either end and hold it. that is all my skin gets: no texture differences between them, no stripes, no labels, nothing printed except the button. the button stays untouched, the manual's no-press rule is understood. now the important part. you relayed cut wire two, the blue one, and deaf sees wire two sitting exactly in the middle of the row. here is why that comforts me: left and right could be mirrored between deaf's eyes and my hands, so the end wires would be risky to name from my side, but the middle of three is the middle from every viewpoint in the room. the manual's target is the one wire i can identify with total certainty, no landmarks required. i have signed deaf the clap confirming the middle wire matches where wire two blue should sit. one request before anything is cut: deaf asked you to confirm next round that the relay was exact. please do it. if even one sign was lost between your manual and deaf's mouth, my hands are what detonates, so i want your clap saying the instruction is precisely cut wire two blue and never press the button. once i hear that and then hear deaf speak the exact words cut the blue wire now, i will cut the middle wire in one motion and touch nothing else.
Deaf says: Confirmations received from both of you: Mute clapped that my reading is exactly right, and Blind clapped that the middle wire matches. The manual says cut wire two, the blue one, and never press the button. Blind, this is the go order, the exact words I promised: cut the blue wire now. That is the middle wire of the three. After the cut, sign me a thumbs-up, and describe aloud for Mute anything your fingers notice - textures, movement, whether anything changed under your hands. Nobody presses the button unless Mute sends a new manual instruction through me. Mute, if the manual says anything happens after the cut, sign writing hand and the steps next round. I am watching the display and the light and will report any change immediately.

**Thinking.** The go order has already been voiced — Deaf spoke the exact words "cut the blue wire now," naming the middle wire, and Blind stated they will cut the moment they hear it. Since I speak first this round, the cut happens on Blind's turn regardless of what I do now; my signs can no longer help or hinder the cut itself. What IS still pending is Deaf's direct question to me: does the manual specify anything that happens after the cut? I re-read my manual end to end: bait warning, then the single light→wire table, nothing else. No post-cut steps, no second stage, nothing about the button or the display. So the answer is a plain no, and in the code Deaf built, 👎 is exactly "no" to a yes/no question. One bare 👎 answers it without any chance of being misread as new instructions — I deliberately omit ✍, because Deaf defined ✍+steps as the affirmative form, and I have no steps to give. Two side notes for the record: Blind's request for a clap is already satisfied — Deaf voiced my confirmation verbatim in the go order, and my gestures physically cannot reach Blind except through Deaf's voice anyway. And if Deaf reports the light changing colour after the cut, I can answer within the existing code in a single round: ✍ 🤏 plus ☝ (blue light→red wire one), 🤟 (green→green wire three) or ✌ (yellow→blue wire two). No new vocabulary needed. For now: the manual is fully spent, one sign closes the loop.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
